stories.title: First Human Trial to Slash Bad Cholesterol by 50% With One Injection of CRISPR Gene-Editing Therapy
stories.label: health
stories.summary: Doctors at the Cleveland Clinic in Ohio tried a one-time CRISPR gene-editing treatment to lower dangerous cholesterol in people who struggle with it. A single infusion cut their bad cholesterol by about 52 percent. A year later, the patients were still enjoying that benefit, and no side effects were reported. It was an early-stage trial, but it shows that one treatment could someday replace a lifetime of daily pills.
stories.why_good: A single treatment actually lowered cholesterol by half for a full year with no side effects, which could one day protect many people from heart disease.

stories.title: Breath of a Whale Captured by Drone Allows Full Genome Sequencing Without Intrusion
stories.label: science
stories.summary: Scientists have found a gentle new way to learn a whale's genetic secrets: they simply catch its breath. Drones flew over the whales and collected the mist from their blowholes. That mist carried enough genetic material for researchers to complete a whole genome sequence of one of these ocean giants, a first. A team from the University of St. Andrews in Scotland took part in the international effort. The whales never had to be touched, tagged, or disturbed.
stories.why_good: It's a real scientific first that lets us study and protect whales without stressing them.
